[{"content":"{\"full_source_conversation\":\"seeker: Hey, can I talk to you about something that's been on my mind?\\nsupporter: Of course, Sarah. What's been happening?\\nseeker: I found out recently that my close friend has been dealing with depression, and it's really worrying me.\\nsupporter: I'm sorry to hear that. It must be difficult to know someone you care about is struggling. How are you handling it?\\nseeker: Honestly, I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed. I want to help but I'm not sure how.\\nsupporter: Wanting to support your friend shows how much you care. It's okay not to have all the answers. Have you been able to talk to them about it?\\nseeker: We talked a little. They admitted things have been tough but didn’t go into much detail. I don’t want to push them.\\nsupporter: It's great that they opened up to you a bit. Listening can be very supportive too. Have you been able to share some of what you're feeling with your therapist?\\nseeker: Yeah, I mentioned it in therapy, but I feel guilty for focusing on my own feelings when my friend is the one struggling.\\nsupporter: Your feelings are valid too, Sarah. It’s natural to feel for your friend, but taking care of yourself is important. It helps you to be there for them.\\nseeker: That makes sense. I guess I'm just scared of making things worse, you know?\\nsupporter: That’s a common fear, but being there for your friend and offering a listening ear can do a lot of good. Have you noticed any changes in how you both interact since you found out?\\nseeker: I’m trying to be more present when we're together. I feel like they've become more withdrawn, and it hurts to see.\\nsupporter: It's tough seeing someone you care about in pain. But showing up and letting them know they're not alone is supportive.\\nseeker: I’ll keep that in mind. I just wish there was more I could do.\\nsupporter: Your friend is lucky to have someone as caring as you. When you're ready, maybe suggesting they talk to a professional could help.\\nseeker: That’s a good point. Maybe I'll bring it up gently if the time feels right. It just feels like there’s so much to balance between work, therapy, and now worrying about my friend.\\nsupporter: It's a lot to juggle, for sure. Remember, you're not alone in this. How has work been since you started therapy?\\nseeker: It's gotten better, slowly. I’m trying to set boundaries and leave work at the office.\\nsupporter: That sounds like progress. It's so important to set boundaries for your well-being. Do you feel therapy has helped you in that regard?\\nseeker: Definitely. Having someone to talk to about these things has been grounding. I just need to remind myself to practice what I'm learning.\\nsupporter: It's wonderful to hear therapy is helping. Implementing what you’ve learned can take time, so be patient with yourself.\\nseeker: Thanks. I’ll try to be kinder to myself. I really appreciate you listening and offering advice.\\nsupporter: Anytime, Sarah. Remember, you're doing your best, and that counts for a lot. Don't hesitate to reach out again if you need to talk.\\nseeker: Thanks again. I’ll definitely reach out.
